transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. I suppose I’m here because I’ve been having some trouble keeping my attention where it’s meant to be. It’s not that I’m not trying — I’ll sit down with a stack of essays to mark, or a curriculum document, fully intending to get through it, and then maybe ten minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page. My mind’s off on three other things, and I’ve barely taken in what’s in front of me.

It’s a bit embarrassing to say, especially with my job, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should ask about it.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Um… not especially, I don’t think. I mean, I might shift in my chair or tap a pen now and then, but I wouldn’t say I feel constantly restless or like I can’t sit still. At least, not in a way that’s really stood out to me. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you often act on impulse or do things without thinking them through?

I don’t think so, not in any major way. I mean, everyone says something a bit too quickly sometimes, don’t they? But I wouldn’t say I’m generally impulsive or doing risky things without thinking. At least, nothing that’s felt like a big issue to me. Does that sound relevant to what you’re asking?
Have you noticed any difficulties with organization or time management in your daily tasks?

Yes… I think so, though I’m a bit reluctant to make it sound worse than it is. It’s not like everything is falling apart, but I do forget ordinary things more than I’d like to admit.

Like, I’ll mean to reply to a parent’s email and then realize later I never did, or I’ll miss paying a bill until the late notice shows up. And at home, my wife might ask me to pick something up on the way back, and unless I write it down immediately, there’s a decent chance I’ll come home without it.

I know those probably sound like normal lapses, but it feels like they happen often enough that it’s becoming a bit awkward.
Did you have a lot of energy or difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

I’m not really sure, to be honest. I don’t remember being the kind of child who was bouncing off the walls or constantly getting told to sit down. I think I was probably fairly normal in that sense.

I mean, my memory of childhood isn’t perfect, and I suppose parents or teachers might remember it differently, but nothing obvious comes to mind about having loads of energy or not being able to sit still. Does that answer it enough?
Do you often feel overwhelmed by your emotions or have trouble calming down after something upsetting happens?

I wouldn’t say that’s a major problem for me, no. I mean, I can get upset like anyone, especially if something stressful happens, but I don’t think I’m losing control of my emotions or anything like that.

I might need a bit of time to cool off sometimes, but it doesn’t feel unusual to me. Unless you mean something more specific by trouble calming down?
Do you have difficulty waiting for your turn in line or waiting for things you want?

Not especially, no. I mean, I don’t love waiting in queues, but I don’t think I’m worse than most people with that.

If I’m waiting for something I want, I might get a bit impatient internally, but I’m not usually interrupting people or pushing ahead or anything like that. I’d say it’s pretty normal, unless there’s something specific you’re looking for there.
Have you noticed difficulties with focusing or completing tasks in both your work and personal life?

Yeah… I think that probably is where it shows up more, actually. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not doing my job or anything, because I do care and I try hard, but at work I’ve had enough missed follow-through on things that my department chair has put me on a support plan.

And at home it’s similar, I suppose. My wife has started taking over things like bills and reminders because she doesn’t really feel she can count on me to keep track of them consistently. That’s a bit embarrassing to say, but yes, it does affect both. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you experienced difficulties with attention or completing tasks since childhood?

Yes, I think so… though at the time it was mostly framed as me being a bit careless rather than anything serious.

Even in primary school, my report cards would say things like I was bright, but careless, or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping a close eye on me. And my parents were always finding worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d done, or partly done, but just forgotten to hand in.

I’m not sure if that counts as what you mean, but looking back it does seem like a similar pattern.
Have you experienced difficulties with attention or completing tasks consistently throughout your childhood and into adulthood?

Yes, I think it has been pretty consistent, looking back. I mean, I did manage, so it didn’t always seem like a major problem at the time, but even in primary school my reports would say things like “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping a close eye on me.

And my parents used to find worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d done, or partly done, and just… forgotten to hand in. So yes, I suppose it’s not something that only started recently. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you often feel excessively fidgety or restless when you're in quiet environments, like meetings or when you're reading?

Not really, no… at least I wouldn’t describe myself as excessively fidgety. I might shift around a bit in a long meeting like anyone would, but I don’t think I’m usually restless in that way.

With reading, it’s more that my mind can wander, but I’m not sure that’s the same as feeling physically unable to sit still. Does that make sense?
Were you more active or restless than your peers when you were a child?

I don’t think so, no. I wasn’t really one of those kids who was always running around or couldn’t sit still, at least not more than other children as far as I remember.

If anything, I think people saw me more as a bit daydreamy than hyperactive… but I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you’re asking about.
Have your difficulties with attention and completing tasks caused you significant stress or problems in your relationships or daily life?

Yes… I mean, I’ve tried not to make a big deal of it, because I do care and I’m not trying to be unreliable. But it has caused problems.

At work, the follow-through side has got serious enough that my department chair put me on a support plan. That was pretty embarrassing, honestly. And at home, my wife has started taking over things like bills and reminders because she doesn’t really trust that I’ll keep track of them consistently.

So… yes, I suppose it’s affecting daily life more than I’d like to admit. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you experienced these attention difficulties consistently over the past few years?

I’d say it’s been more noticeable over the last… maybe 11 months or so. It wasn’t like it suddenly appeared, but since the school changed the curriculum calendar and added those after-school planning meetings, it’s definitely been harder to keep on top of things.

I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when it started feeling more consistently like a problem rather than just the odd busy week, if that makes sense.
Have you experienced these attention difficulties for more than 6 months?

Yes, it has been more than six months. I’d put it at around 11 months where it’s been noticeably worse — since the school changed the curriculum calendar and added those after-school planning meetings.

I mean, I’ve probably had some version of it before, but in terms of it being a consistent problem, yes… about 11 months.
Have you experienced these attention difficulties consistently since childhood?

Yes… I think so, although I probably would have described it back then as just being a bit careless or disorganized.

Even in primary school, my report cards would say things like, “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was closely supervising me. And my parents were always finding worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d forgotten to turn in.

I suppose I didn’t think of it as an attention issue at the time, but looking back, yes, there were signs pretty early on. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you experienced significant difficulties with attention for at least 6 months?

Yes, I think so. I mean, it’s been noticeably worse for about 11 months now — since the school changed the curriculum calendar and added those after-school planning meetings.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but yes, it’s definitely been going on longer than six months.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with attention for your entire life?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but even in primary school my report cards used to say things like “bright but careless,” or “doesn’t finish work unless closely supervised.”

And my parents were always finding worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d forgotten to turn in. At the time it just seemed like I was messy or not trying hard enough, but looking back, it does feel like it’s been there most of my life.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with attention since before the age of 12?

Yes, I think so. I mean, I don’t remember exact ages perfectly, but in primary school it was already showing up.

My report cards used to say things like “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was closely supervising me. And my parents would find worksheets all crumpled up in my backpack that I’d forgotten to hand in.

At the time I think everyone just saw it as me being a bit messy or not trying hard enough, but… yes, I’d say it was there before 12.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with attention for at least 6 months, consistently across most areas of life?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to exaggerate it, but it’s been noticeably worse for about 11 months now, since the school changed the curriculum calendar and added those after-school planning meetings.

So yes, definitely more than six months. I hope that answers what you mean by consistently.
